note_on_method: Each venue page rests on the City of Tampa's pickleball page - one card per venue, with a label, a name, an address and a count, dated "Updated: 10/28/2025" - and, where the address is also a community centre, on the City's recreation-centres list for the phone number and the "Features:" line. The US Census address geocoder and OpenStreetMap supply the county and the postcode. Where the City is silent, these pages record the silence; where the Census changed a compass direction or a street type, they say which resolver's answer is published and why.

slots.description:
Four outdoor pickleball courts in East Tampa, on a card the City writes in three lines: "Al Barnes Park / 2902 N 32nd St, Tampa, 33605 / 4 courts", under the label "Outdoor Pickleball". That is the entire published record of pickleball at this park. The City's pickleball page is a grid of cards, and Al Barnes gets the plainest kind - no hours, no session, no note, just an address and a number - which puts it in the majority in Tampa, where nine of the twelve outdoor cards say nothing beyond the count.

Four courts is a workable number: two games at once, or a group of eight rotating without much waiting. The park has no entry on the City's recreation-centres list, so unlike Copeland or Forest Hills there is no building, gym or phone number attached to the address in the City records this site has read.

The pickleball page names a contact for the whole programme rather than for this park - a Site Supervisor at 59 Columbia Drive, 813-712-0321 - and that is the nearest thing to a phone number Al Barnes has.

2902 N 32nd St, Tampa, FL 33605. The address is the City's, and it resolves through OpenStreetMap rather than the US Census address file, which holds no record of it; OpenStreetMap matches it at house-number level on North 32nd Street, in the East Ybor area, in Hillsborough County and inside the incorporated city of Tampa. It is one of four Tampa venues that needed the second resolver.

The City publishes nothing about parking at this park, nothing about restrooms, and nothing about how to reach it by any means. This site does not fill those in.
slots.what_to_expect:
Four courts, outdoors, and a City record that stops there. Hours are not stated, so this site cannot tell you whether the park is a sunrise-to-sunset park like Madison Street and Vila Brothers or something else; lighting is not stated, so evening play is an open question rather than a yes or a no; price is not stated, and this site records no fee answer rather than assuming free. Surface is not stated either.

What the City does establish, by the label on the card, is that these are outdoor courts. Cuscaden Park, in the same 33605 postcode, is the East Tampa venue with a stated session - senior open play on Wednesday mornings - and Al Barnes has none. With no published open-play time, there is nothing on the City's record to suggest a rotation forms here on its own, so bring a group. Four courts is enough for two games and a short wait, which is more than half of Tampa's outdoor venues can offer.
